cells.tense: You are reading what is really out there, and you are making moves on it.
cells.ask: Lay one guess about next week out loud for someone, and let them push on it before you defend it.
cells.core:
You sense what's moving in a room before anyone names it — the shifty mood, the live idea, the door about to open — and that reading comes with a move attached. Not noise you're managing. Direction you're setting.

It has a texture. Pictures that surface get acted on instead of stored, and the choices hold past the week they were made in. You trust the flow before it's proved, then check the outcome and adjust without drama. Full of ideas and moving is a different life from full of ideas and frozen. Keep one eye on where it's heading, though. The supply comes from somewhere, and finding out it dried up is a worse way to learn where it came from.

cells.tense: You're somewhere in next week already, running moves that haven't happened yet.
cells.ask: Ask what will actually happen this week, follow that one answer, and let the second guess go.
cells.core:
The scanning is out in front of you now. You're not reading the room — you're rehearsing the rooms after it, three moves deep, settling things you can't see yet and bracing for endings with no date on them. Somewhere under that, a fear keeps dressing as a hunch, and the evidence doesn't come up to meet it.

When worrying runs this far ahead, the pictures have no ground to land on. What looks like foresight is worry with a to-do list. Slow one thing down — if it still reads true in a week, move on it. If it won't hold still, that's the dread talking, and dread doesn't get a vote on Tuesday.

cells.tense: The reading is still in you, but your hand hasn't moved in a long time.
cells.ask: Let yourself not know something for a few minutes, then say one plain sentence about why something matters to you.
cells.core:
The moves quit happening first. You notice the live idea and the quiet pull, and then you don't act on it, don't say it, don't write it down, and the not-doing has come to look like calm. The sense of what could be is intact; it's the doing that went quiet.

When this works, you do one small thing with what surfaces instead of waiting to feel sure — you write the sentence, you make the call, you say the plain thing and check it later. You can't manufacture wanting, so don't try. Let the actual weight of something land for once, clear-eyed and unhurried. One corner of the picture can be true without fitting into any plan.
cells.sheetLine: The vision is still in there and the acting on it stopped.
cells.verb: trusting what rises before it has a name

cells.tense: You are writing the next move all the time, but saying it belongs to the room.
cells.ask: Pick the one thing you're steering this week and say out loud that it was your call.
cells.core:
Something is being chosen here, and the telling of it keeps landing on the room. What you keep, what you drop, the pictures you act on in a team or a family — the picking is running, and the credit keeps going somewhere else. The lines are drawn. You just won't sign them.

Say 'that was my call' about one thing you're currently calling the work's or the group's. What's moving is settling itself, you keep saying, and you keep being the one who moves it. The thinking is already yours. Practice, plain and unforced, shows you that — not the kind that has to prove you saw your own hand on the tiller.
cells.sheetLine: You are moving on what you're already picking. Say it.

attempts.check: The record supports the draft directly: this card sits in the choosing-capacity, and the watchfulness/lateness that steer each ask follow from the Failure and Consideration bounds themselves. What a reader could reasonably object to is the Too Little portrait sealing 'someone said no' into who they are, when the dropout could be long carrying or depression; the mirror word choice ('the no') may not match their wording. The ask survives a wrong read — the twelve-minute 'what might happen Wednesday' touching one burdened supply chain spends no money and needs no one, so a misread gets a useful hour back regardless. The sentence serving the writer more than the person is 'somebody said this was safer than the wanting' — a story dropped on them rather than one handed back.
